additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh carreg 'stone, rock' (Carrick, Crick); a prominent stone or crag.

additions.gloss: A grove, a copse, a small wood.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh celli 'grove, copse' (Kelly, -gelli); a small woodland.

additions.gloss: A hillock, a knoll, a rounded hill.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic/Goidelic cnocc 'hillock' (Knock-, -nock); a small rounded hill.

additions.gloss: Crooked, bent, curved.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh crwm 'crooked, curved'; a curving feature (Crom-, -crum).

additions.gloss: A valley, a coomb, a deep hollow.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *cumbo- > Welsh cwm 'valley' (Combe, -cum); a steep-sided hollow.

additions.gloss: An oak; an oak-wood.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *dervā 'oak' (Derwent 'oak-river', Darwen); oak-tree element.

additions.gloss: A mouth, an opening; the mouth of a valley or pass.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh genau 'mouth, opening' (Genau-, -gena); a defile or valley-mouth.

additions.gloss: An elm-tree; element in river-names.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *lemano- 'elm' (Leman, Lymn, Leamington); elm-named watercourse.

additions.gloss: Bald, bare; a bare rounded hill.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *mailo- 'bald' > Welsh moel; a bare-topped hill (Mellor, Malvern).

additions.gloss: Pigs, swine; a swine-pasture.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh moch 'pigs' (Mochdre, -moch); a place where swine were kept.

additions.gloss: Big, great.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *māro- > Welsh mawr 'big'; an intensifier on a place-element.

additions.gloss: A valley, a brook-valley, a dell.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic nans/nant 'valley' (Nant-, -nance); a small steep valley with a stream.

additions.gloss: A sacred grove, a sanctuary.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic *nemeton 'sacred grove' (Nymet, Nempnett); a pre-Christian cult site.

additions.gloss: A boar, a hog; also a mole.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Welsh twrch 'boar' (Twrch, river-names); a rooting animal or burrowing stream.

additions.gloss: A wood, a forest; also a dwelling-place.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Brittonic wīg (Welsh gwig 'wood' < Latin vīcus 'settlement'); wooded or settled spot.

additions.gloss: A rock, a crag, a cliff.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Goidelic creag/crag 'rock' (Craig-, -craig); a prominent rock or cliff.

additions.gloss: A Celtic derivational/adjectival suffix (-oscus).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latinised Celtic -oscus ending in Romano-British derived names (parallel to -iscus).

additions.gloss: Little; a small portion or smallholding.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Goidelic beagán 'a little' (Beggan, -beg); a small parcel of land.

additions.gloss: A Latin derivational/adjectival suffix (-ascus).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latinised -ascus ending in Romano-British derived names (parallel to -iscus/-oscus).

additions.gloss: A Roman gentile name (Gallius).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latin nomen Gallius, underlying a Romano-British estate-name (fundus Gallianus → -).

additions.gloss: A Roman gentile name (Granius).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latin nomen Granius, underlying a Romano-British estate-name.

additions.gloss: A Latin nominal/gentile suffix (-ius).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latin -ius forms gentile names and derivatives in Romano-British estate-names.

additions.gloss: A Roman gentile name (Marcius).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Latin nomen Marcius, underlying a Romano-British estate-name (fundus Marcianus).

additions.gloss: A copse, a coppiced wood, a thicket.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Modern English copse (< OFr copeiz); a small wood grown for periodic cutting.

additions.gloss: A hill; a natural elevation of the land.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Modern English hill (< OE hyll); a generic raised landform.

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name (Ada/Æd(d)a).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE personal name Ada, forming -ing/-ton habitative compounds.

additions.gloss: An alderman, a chief; a nobleman of high rank.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE ealdormann 'chief, nobleman' (Aldermaston, -alderman); a shire's leading man.

additions.gloss: A heathen temple, a sanctuary; a protected place.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE ealh/alh 'temple, sanctuary' (Alkham, -alh); pre-Christian cult site.

additions.gloss: A ball; a rounded hill or knoll.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE *ball 'rounded mass' (Balls-, -ball); a knoll or ball-shaped rise.

additions.gloss: An Old English byname, 'the pale/dark one'.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE blæca (a personal byname from blæc 'pale/black'); -ing/-ton names.

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name (Bosa).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE personal name Bosa, forming habitative compounds (Boston < Bosa's tun?).

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name, Beorhthelm ('bright helmet').
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE dithematic name Beorhthelm/Brihthelm; underlies -ton/-ham names.

additions.gloss: The site of a stronghold; a fortified place, a castle-stead.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE burh-stall 'site of a fort' (Borstal, Burstall); the place where a burh stood.

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name, Ceadda (St Chad).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE personal name Cedda/Ceadda; underlies Chadwell, Chadderton.

additions.gloss: A turning, a bend in a road or river.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE cerring 'a turning' (from cerr); a bend-place (Charing, -charn).

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name, Ēadwulf ('prosperity-wolf').
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE dithematic name Ēadwulf; underlies Edwalton, - wulf habitative names.

additions.gloss: A half; a side, a slope of land.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE half/healf 'half, side' (Halnaby, -half); a side or division of land.

additions.gloss: An Old English personal name (Otta).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE personal name Otta; underlies Ottershaw, Otterton(?)-type -ing/-ton names.

additions.gloss: A sheep-wash; a place in a stream for washing sheep.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE scēap-wæsce 'sheep-washing place' (Shipwash, -wash).

additions.gloss: A personal name, Thurstan (< ON Þorsteinn 'Thor-stone').
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Anglo-Scandinavian name Thurstan; underlies Thurstonland, -thwaite.

additions.gloss: The source of a river, a spring.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE ǣwelm/ǣwielm 'river-source' (Ewelme, Emble); where a stream rises.

additions.gloss: An Old Norse personal name (Ási).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: ON personal name Ási; underlies -by/-thorpe Danelaw names (Asby, Asenby).

additions.gloss: A bank, a slope; a ridge or hillside.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: ON banke/bakki 'bank, slope' (-bank, Firbank); a sloping bank or ridge.

additions.gloss: A brink, a steep slope; the edge of a hill.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: ON brink/brekka 'slope, hill-edge' (Brink-, -brink); a steep declivity.

additions.gloss: An Irish personal name; a saint's name (Farannán).
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: Goidelic Farannán, an early Irish saint-name; underlies eccles/kil- dedications.

additions.gloss: Hay; mown or dried grass.
additions.reason: wyrd-eni4.3 gloss tail: OE filiðe/feleðe 'hay' (Filey?, hay-meadow element); a place yielding hay.
